A1.reason: split_work_to_cores(row_wise=True) is applied, but on a 130-core grid the op uses 128 cores, so row-wise and column-wise select almost the same set and the DRAM-facing spread is identical. Delta is inside noise on every bench shape (grid_filling -0.6%, row_major -0.9%, smallest -1.4%). Kept on: it costs nothing and it is the right default the moment the op runs on a partial grid. RE-MEASURED under the refinement-1 topology: still inside noise at the bfloat16 loose corner (91201 ON vs 89684 OFF, i.e. column-wise is 1.7% FASTER there), but on bfloat8_b the applied row-wise arm is 1.045x better (71273 vs 74486) - the first regime where the DRAM-facing spread is visible at all, consistent with bfloat8_b halving the bytes per core and making placement relatively more important. Kept ON; the verdict stays measured-no-payoff because the two corners disagree at the few-percent level, and it is worth re-checking once Lamp L3 puts the op on a partial grid.

A2.reason: Launch only on cores that hold data requires a sharded input; Phase 0 SUPPORTED[memory_layout] is INTERLEAVED only, so there are no shard-owning cores to launch on.

A3.reason: Interleaved pages are spread over every DRAM bank by the TensorAccessor, so a core cannot be made adjacent to 'its' bank; only the A1 axis spread is expressible. A3 becomes real once the input is sharded (each core then owns one bank's worth of rows).
A3.followup: With Lamp L3 sharding, map each shard to its NoC-optimal worker (get_optimal_worker_cores_for_sharded_tensor).

A4.reason: The remainder is handled by split_work_to_cores' two core groups and by padding the final row-block to a full BLOCK_HT (phantom tile-rows clamped to the last valid one), so no core is idle - but there is no specialised cliff kernel, and the cliff core still pays for BLOCK_HT tile-rows of work when it owns fewer.

B6.reason: UNLOCKED by refinement-1 and re-measured. Phase 0 closed B6 measured-no-payoff because, at a 2048 B bfloat16 tile, splitting the page bought nothing beyond what B5 already measured. Adding bfloat8_b moved that premise: a bfloat8_b tile is 1088 B, so the same whole-page transaction now saves relatively more, and the OFF arm costs 1.129x on grid_filling at bfloat8_b (71273 -> 80440 ns) versus 1.087x at the bfloat16 loose corner (91201 -> 99102). The knob was already applied, so this is a stronger justification for the existing default rather than new work. Refinement 1 also had to FIX the counterfactual to measure this honestly: the off-arm split the page at IN_TILE_BYTES/2, which is 544 B for bfloat8_b - not a multiple of Blackhole's 64 B DRAM alignment, so the second transfer was illegal. Rounding the first half down to a 64 B multiple (1088 -> 512 + 576) makes both offsets legal, and the corrected arm reports 1.129x where the illegal one reported 1.249x - i.e. the unaligned access was inflating the win by 11 points.

B8.reason: MEASURED in Perf 1 and refuted, on the bench gap phase-0 flagged (blocks-per-core > 1 now exists: the focus shape issues 4 read groups per dispatch and wide_prefill 2 row-blocks per core). `..._with_trid` costs +5.5 ns/txn over plain state reuse (22.1 vs 16.6 ns/txn of issue, from the NIU_MST_REQS_OUTSTANDING_ID poll in ncrisc_noc_fast_read_with_transaction_id) which is MORE than the barrier it could hide (3.1 ns/txn in the op's rd_in_barrier). It composes correctly with B13's state reuse and is bit-exact, but the surcharge cancels the overlap. The deeper reason it cannot pay here is the same one that killed B13: the reader is not issue-bound, it is at the per-core NoC/DRAM service ceiling of ~29 ns per 2 KB page (~70 GB/s), so there is no barrier time for a double-issue to reclaim. The cross-block pipelined form (>=2-chunk lookahead reserve) was NOT built; its ceiling on the focus shape is the 693-1446 ns of rd_in_barrier, and after the W split that is divided by the group size.

measured.note: isolated reader, 224 x 2048 B interleaved tile pages, 1 core, chunk 112, one barrier per chunk. ON = noc_async_read_tile_with_trid + barrier on the previous id, OFF = the same stateful read without a trid.

B10.reason: Per-reader virtual-channel assignment is only meaningful once several readers share a route; with 128 cores each reading interleaved pages from all banks the routes are already spread, and B9 already removed the read/write contention that dominates.

B11.reason: Every DRAM address this op forms is alignment-legal by construction: tile transfers go through TensorAccessor's aligned page stride, and the two byte-offset paths (RM stick W-chunk, RM gamma slice) use offsets that are multiples of 32*element_size (>= 64 B). There is no misaligned variant to measure - one is a hardware fault, not a slower arm. The acceptance suite run under --dev (NoC sanitizer on) is the mechanical pin: it caught exactly this class of bug when an earlier gamma path issued a read at stick offset +32 B on a 64 B-aligned device. RE-CONFIRMED under the refinement-1 topology: adding bfloat8_b changes the tile page size to 1088 B but every tile transfer still goes through TensorAccessor's aligned page stride, and the two byte-offset paths remain ROW_MAJOR-only - which a block format cannot be (ttnn refuses to build a ROW_MAJOR bfloat8_b tensor), asserted in blocking_plan(). So no new address arithmetic was introduced and there is still no misaligned variant to measure.

B12.reason: APPLIED in Perf 1, though not in the form phase 0 predicted. Phase 0 filed B12 as 'read gamma once on an injector core and mcast it', sized at a 5.3% upper bound. Two Perf-1 measurements moved that: (a) the whole-page gamma read that made the replication expensive is gone (the reader now fetches only the row-0 span, 544 B of a 2048 B page), which shrank the gamma-mcast ceiling to <= 8.7%; and (b) a multicast DID graduate, on a different operand - the cross-core W-split combine broadcasts the summed sum-of-squares 1->N with mcast_pipe's SenderPipe/ReceiverPipe. That leg was benched against the alternative the catalog names (N-1 unicasts + semaphore increments) and the multicast wins at every group size: 10161 vs 10730 at G=14 (-5.3%), 10368 vs 12016 at G=56 (-13.7%). The hand-rolled arm was dropped from the shipped op. The design's all-mcast variant (every core broadcasts to every other, G^2 transfers instead of 2G) stays rejected on fan-out and was not re-tested. The gamma-mcast form remains open with a measured ceiling; it also has a structural blocker worth recording - split_work_to_cores gives cores DIFFERENT row-block counts, so the per-chunk gamma round count differs per core and a naive SenderPipe/ReceiverPipe handshake deadlocks (the sender waits for a round only some receivers reach).

measured.note: the W-split combine's 1->N broadcast leg at group size 14. ON = mcast_pipe SenderPipe/ReceiverPipe; OFF = a hand-rolled fan-out of group_size-1 unicast writes + semaphore increments. Whole-op device kernel duration, so the delta is the combine leg only.
measured.gamma_mcast_ceiling_note: the SEPARATE gamma-mcast idea (read gamma once on an injector, broadcast to the group) was BOUNDED by measurement and not built: an inject_only ceiling probe (span read on one core, all others issuing nothing, every core's CB lifecycle intact) caps it at <= +5.1% on (1,1,8192,1024) (94276 -> 89496) and <= +8.7% on (1,1,8192,7168) (1031582 -> 942181), and at 0% on the focus shape, which runs one gamma reader per group.

B13.reason: MEASURED in Perf 1, and the phase-0 prediction of 5% was right about the mechanism and wrong about the sign. Splitting the lever into its two halves is what made it legible. (a) The ACTUAL state-reuse mechanism REGRESSES: `with_state` republishes only TARG/RET_ADDR_LO, so it requires BANK-MAJOR issue order, and bank-major serialises DRAM channels - a core fires 14-112 back-to-back requests at one bank instead of spreading them. Measured: (1,1,8192,1024) read 42420 -> 49607 (+17%), the widest shape 295887 -> 405266 (+37%), fp32 writes 12008 -> 17639 (+47%), (32,17) 724 -> 790 (+9%, the B0 regime). A per-core bank rotation recovers only part of it, so the cause is intra-core bank concentration, not cross-core phase alignment. It INVERTS at bfloat8_b's 1088 B tiles (read 7816 -> 5002, -36%; write 8419 -> 4709, -44%) where the transaction rate genuinely is the limit - a real dtype-gated dual path, recorded and NOT shipped, because a dual path is debt. (b) The ORDER-PRESERVING half of the same idea - passing a compile-time size bound so the runtime any-length dispatch loop disappears - is a clean 13-14% on the isolated reader/writer (8028 -> 6980 read, 8606 -> 7578 write) and IS APPLIED: noc_async_read_tile / noc_async_write_tile are deleted from both kernels. The corrected diagnosis is the durable finding: the reader/writer are NOT issue-bound but sit at the per-core NoC/DRAM service ceiling of ~29 ns per 2 KB page each way (~70 GB/s), and the baseline issued at 30.7 ns/txn, just above that rate - which is why the zones read 'issue hot, barrier ~ 0'. Cutting issue to 16.8 ns/txn puts it BELOW the service rate, so the saving moves ns-for-ns from rd_in_issue into rd_in_barrier (measured whole-op on (1,1,8192,1024): rd_in_issue 5763 -> 4904, rd_in_barrier 14648 -> 15233) instead of becoming throughput. It only surfaces where a core is issue-serialised rather than DRAM-serialised: (1,1,32,4095) 1.062x, (1,1,100,736) 1.028x.

measured.note: isolated reader, 8192 pages over 64 cores. ON = noc_async_read_one_packet_set_state + ..._with_state in the bank-major order state reuse REQUIRES; OFF = the op's round-robin page order. The lever COSTS 17% here.

C14.reason: Zero-copy aliasing of a CB onto a shard buffer requires a sharded input; Phase 0 is interleaved-only.
C14.followup: Lamp L3: ttnn.cb_descriptor_from_sharded_tensor(CB_INPUT_TILES, input_tensor) once HEIGHT_SHARDED is in SUPPORTED - no NoC read at all for the resident rows.

C15.reason: Same gate as C14/A2: the op is DRAM-interleaved in Phase 0, so it cannot take the L1-resident path. The measured ablation says this is where the money is on the prefill shapes - stubbing the NoC payload on (1,1,8192,1024) drops the op to 26% of its full time.
C15.followup: Lamp L3 (HEIGHT_SHARDED) then Lamp L1 (WIDTH/BLOCK_SHARDED with the cross-core combine).

C16.reason: REFUTED AND RE-CLOSED in Perf 1 with new arms, under this phase. The phase-0/refinement-1 verdict of measured-no-payoff was honest but was measured on the DRAM-saturated (1,1,8192,1024) shape, and on a wide Regime-B shape its two arms were the SAME PROGRAM: the solver already produced depth 1 there, so forcing depth 1 changed nothing and the lever was never actually tested. The cumulative ablation is what exposed it - the focus case came out ADDITIVE (full 43983 ~ stub_dm 28221 + stub_compute 24093 - floor 9230), i.e. ~0% reader/compute overlap, on a plan where every streaming CB was depth 1. The cause was the solver's step ORDER, not a missing knob: it took the coarsest W-chunk that fits at depth 1 and then tried to double-buffer inside whatever L1 was left, which on a wide shape is nothing. Subordinating the chunk search to the depth profile captures 62% of the available overlap (rd_gamma_reserve 6396 -> 146 ns, rd_in_reserve 3100 -> 306, wr_wait 34982 -> 23784) at LESS L1 (1155072 -> 811008 B). Note the win needs BOTH cb_input_tiles AND cb_gamma_tiles at depth 2 - measured in isolation at chunk 56: all-depth-1 0.94x, output-only 0.94x, input-only 1.02x, gamma-only 1.18x, input+gamma 1.36x - and cb_gamma_tiles was hard-coded to depth 1 in _cb_layout, which is why no arm of the old knob could reach it. Also measured: the search is NOT monotone in the L1 budget (freeing L1 moves 'coarsest that fits' coarser, and coarser is not always better), so the profile it asks for is the depth ladder's top rung; three profiles were compared and remain live arms.

measured.note: ON = the W-chunk search subordinated to CB depth (coarsest divisor of Wt_core at which the streaming profile in/out/rm/gamma fits); OFF = the pre-Perf-1 ordering, coarsest chunk that fits at DEPTH 1 first, then double-buffer whatever L1 is left. A/B in one tree with the old _solve monkeypatched back, so no sibling change leaks in.

C17.reason: rms_norm is not an in-place op on its public contract - it allocates a fresh output tensor. Writing into the input buffer would need a caller opt-in, and the input is still being read in pass B of Regime B.
C17.followup: Add an `output_tensor=` parameter so a caller can alias, and gate it on Regime A (single-read) where the input is fully consumed before the scale pass writes.

D18.reason: Already in the applied FORM - every TensorAccessorArgs is emitted through get_compile_time_args() and read back with TensorAccessorArgs<N>() in the kernels, so address generation is unrolled per buffer type. What is missing is the counterfactual arm that would close it with a number.
D18.followup: Add a `runtime_accessor_args` arm that passes the accessor args as runtime args and measure on (1,1,8192,1024) and (32,17).

D19.reason: Already in the applied FORM - the only runtime args are buffer base addresses plus the per-core (start_row_block, num_row_blocks) pair and the two fp32 scalar bit patterns; every geometry constant is a compile-time arg. No counterfactual arm yet.
D19.followup: Add an arm that demotes the geometry prefix to runtime args and measure the program-cache re-dispatch cost.

D20.reason: APPLIED in Perf 1. Phase 0 recorded D20 as 'already in the applied FORM' (two structurally different plans behind a pinned host predicate, plus a compile-time TILE/ROW_MAJOR fork) with the follow-up 'add a force_regime arm so the single-read fast path can be priced'. Both halves are now done. Priced: Regime A vs a forced Regime B is 1.32x on (1,1,8192,1024) (118095 vs 155792) and 1.47x on its ROW_MAJOR twin (91492 vs 134005) - the byte model's 1.5x, confirmed. And the selection got a THIRD axis that pays far more than tuning the existing two: _choose_group_size scores every candidate combine-group size with the same solver that will produce the shipped plan, so a shape whose row-parallel plan would be Regime B on one core is re-planned as G cores each running Regime A. That is what takes the focus case from 43947 to 9010 ns (4.88x) and (1,1,8192,7168) from 1229676 to 603971 (2.04x): not only parallelism, but a narrow per-core slice that turns two DRAM reads of x into one and stops replicating gamma. A fourth level was measured and NOT graduated because the W split supersedes it on the shapes that matter: a resident-x ladder (A -> x+gamma resident with normed/out chunked -> x resident with gamma/normed/out chunked -> B) measured 1.419x on the focus case and 1.545x on (1,1,8192,7168) BEFORE the split, against the split's 4.88x and 2.04x. It stays a round-2 candidate for the shapes the split cannot take (non-tile-aligned W, where it would first need the masked variant it does not have).

F23.reason: RE-CLOSED under the refinement-1 topology, with the wording tightened because this phase added the op's only config-touching code. For every REAL call the caller's ComputeConfigDescriptor is still handed to the compute KernelDescriptor verbatim and never rebuilt: the sole rebuild site, _apply_precision_levers(), is reached only from the internal `_levers` bench hook (levers F24 / F25' counterfactual arms), returns the caller's own object identically at the lever defaults, and no public argument can set a lever. The only value the op CHOOSES is its own default, in the single exported default_compute_kernel_config() factory - and refinement 1 did not move it, even though F25/F27 measure the cheaper corner as a win, precisely because F23 forbids it. The named test passes an explicit descriptor and asserts the result; test_rms_norm_default_compute_kernel_config_is_a_factory pins the factory.

F24.reason: RE-CLOSED under the refinement-1 topology. The Phase-0 closure was structurally-impossible on the premise that SUPPORTED[dtype] held no block format, so no bfloat8_b pack existed for the knob to govern; refinement 1 added bfloat8_b, so that premise is void. The applied setting is the CHEAP one, the FAST packer (bfp8_pack_precise stays False): /numeric-formats-metal S1.7 gates the precise packer on a float32 INPUT, and this op's output dtype always equals its input dtype, so a bfloat8_b output implies a bfloat8_b input - never the wide-input case that needs rounding. The accuracy margin confirms it: every bfloat8_b cell of test_rms_norm_precision_matrix passes on the fast packer with min PCC 0.999944 and max rel_rms 0.0132 against a 0.99 gate. Measured both arms anyway: the precise packer is FLAT here (grid_filling fast 71639 vs precise 71267 ns; grid_starved 65997 vs 65977 ns, both inside noise), so the choice carries no perf risk in either direction and rests on the accuracy margin, not on a throughput argument.

F25.reason: Refinement 1 added False to SUPPORTED[fp32_dest_acc_en], which is what Phase 0 deferred F25 on. Attributed ALONE (fidelity held at the default HiFi4, config `dest_off`), the cheap DEST width is 1.06x on the compute-bound decode shape (grid_starved 76079 -> 71823 ns) and flat on the DRAM-bound one (grid_filling 93581 -> 93910 ns, noise) - exactly the split the Phase-0 ablation predicts, since a narrower DEST buys math throughput and cannot create DRAM bandwidth. The `loose` corner's larger 1.58x on grid_starved (76079 -> 47987) is mostly F27: HiFi2 on top of the cheap DEST accounts for 71823 -> 47987. Making the cheap corner CORRECT was the real work, not flipping the flag: at 16-bit DEST, ReduceTile's long per-tile DEST accumulation carries a systematic sum-of-squares overestimate that grows with the reduced width (+0.84% at Wt=32, +1.9% at 64, +5.6% at 128, +10.4% at 224), which surfaced as a uniform ~4.8% low output scale at W=7168 while PCC still read 0.99995. Fixed by routing Regime B to ReduceAlgorithm::AccumulateViaAdd on that path (knob `reduce_via_add`). The op's EXPORTED default stays fp32_dest_acc_en=True per references/precision_convention.md; F23 forbids downgrading a caller-supplied value, so the op offers the cheap corner, it does not impose it.

F26.reason: RE-CLOSED under the refinement-1 topology (which added bfloat8_b, a second reduce datapath and two derived CB formats - none of which creates a lossless-unpack opportunity). A lossless unpack buys nothing downstream of any FPU phase, and every path here hits one: sum_of_squares and both scale multiplies are FPU binaries, reduce<SUM, REDUCE_ROW> is FPU/GMPOOL on either datapath, and the RM tilize uses the fast route by design. Refinement 1 adds a SECOND, independent disqualifier found while auditing the UnpackToDestFp32 candidates: the only CB that is exclusively copy_tile-reloaded would be cb_sumsq, but reduce()'s accumulator reload reads it through SrcA/SrcB (AccumulateReloadMode::FoldViaAdd and the ReduceTile accumulate), which reduce_helpers_compute.hpp documents as valid ONLY when that CB is UnpackToDestMode::Default - tagging it would be incorrect, not merely slower. cb_rms_recip feeds an FPU broadcast multiply and cb_sumsq_acc feeds the reduce, so neither is eligible either. The float32 test passes at PCC 0.999 on the fast path, so the precision the lever protects is not needed.

F27.reason: NOT changed in Phase 0 or Refinement 1, and still MISSED rather than closed. references/precision_convention.md and the op prompt pin the exported default_compute_kernel_config() to HiFi4, and F23 forbids downgrading a caller-supplied value. Re-measured at the refinement-1 DEST width on the compute-bound decode shape: with fp32_dest_acc_en=False held fixed, HiFi4 71823 ns -> HiFi2 47987 ns = 1.50x (Phase 0 measured 1.45x at the fp32 DEST width), and flat on grid_filling (93581 -> 91003, DRAM-bound). It is the single largest unexploited compute lever on the perf-gated (1,1,32,7168) cell - and note the loose case that carries the 7x gate SUPPLIES HiFi2 itself, so that cell already gets it; the miss is only for callers who leave math_fidelity unset.
